senses.gloss: ch. sameto untie, unharness; to disengage, dismiss.
units: Targ. O. Gen. XXIV, 32 וש׳ גמליא (ed. Berl. וש׳ מן ג׳; Y. ושָׁ׳ זממי ג׳ Pa.; h. text ויפתח).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 30:11">Targ. Job XXX, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 3:5">Targ. O. Ex. III, 5</cite> (h. text <he>של</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 113a:7">Pes. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>שְׁרִי כיסך פתח שפיך</he> untie thy purse (to receive the money), open thy bag (to deliver the goods), i.e. sell for cash.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 98a:16">Snh. 98ᵃ</cite> <he>כולהון שְׁרוֹ ואסירי … איהו ש׳ חד וכ׳</he> all of them untie and tie up (their sores) at once (untie all of them, and then tie them up), but he unties and ties up one at a time.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 22:1">Pesik. R. s. 22</cite> [read:] <he>שַׁרְתַּנְהוֹן … ע״ג סודרא</he> she untied them (the two Denars), and placed them on the shawl.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:5:8">Y. Ber. II, 5ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>אתת … ושַׁרְתוּן וכ׳</he> (fr. <cite ref="U01959"><he>שרה</he></cite>, cmp. <cite ref="H01172"><he>חֲמֵי</he></cite>) when prayer time came, he untied them (the coins), and gave them to R. H.; [read:] <he>קטר פורתיה לפורתיה ויהבון לשמעיה ושרתון וערק</he> he tied his (R. Ḥ’s) share to his own, and gave them to his servant, but he (the servant) untied them and ran away.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:5:3">Y. Meg. IV, 75ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>שְׁרוֹן ליה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="O01431"><he>סַפְרוּתָא</he></cite>.
Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵃ שרון גרמון ומנוניה they dismissed themselves (resigned their office) and appointed him (Hillel) in their place; a. fr.—ש׳ תיגרא to solve a dispute, to settle or decide a case.
<cite ref="Nedarim 62a:12">Ned. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>שְׁרוּ לי תיגראי ברישא</he> take my case up first.
<cite ref="Yevamot 100a:8">Yeb. 100ᵃ</cite> <he>שָׁרֵינָא וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="V00093"><he>תִּגְרָא</he> I</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to allow, permit; to forgive; to absolve (= h. הִתִּיר).
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 30:3">Targ. Y. Num. XXX, 3</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 22:14">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XXII, 14</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 14:20">Targ. Y. II, Num. XIV, 20</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Kiddushin 13b:9">Kidd. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>הוא אסרה והוא שַׁרְתָהּ</he> (Rashi <he>שרי לה</he>) he tied her (by marrying her), and he untied her (through his death, that she can dispose of herself).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:7:3">Y. Ber. II, 5ᵇ</cite> <he>אינון שַׁרְיָין ואינון אסרין</he> do the same men permit and forbid? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7:13:3">Y. Snh. VII, end, 25ᵈ</cite> [read:] <he>שַׁרְיִי מה דעבדתין אמרה ליה לי נא שַׁרְיָיה</he> undo what thou hast done (by charm); said she to him, I will not undo. Bab.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 99a:4">Snh. 99ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ ליה מריה וכ׳</he> the Lord forgive R. Hillel.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 37a:3">Ab. Zar. 37ᵃ</cite> <he>וקרו לן בית דינא שָׁרְיָא</he> and they might call us a permitting court (of lax practice).

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 37a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>כי שְׁרִיתוּהָ לאלתר שריתוה וכ׳</he> when you permitted her (to marry again), did you permit her to marry at once &c.? <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 37a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>וקרו ליה יוסף שריא</he> and they called him Joseph the permitter.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 37a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>אנא נמי שְׁרָאִי אחריתי</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>אנא שרא</he>, corr. acc.) I also permitted another thing (which was forbidden heretofore); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U01961"><he>שָׁרֵי</he></cite>, <cite ref="U01963"><he>שַׁרְיָא</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="U01963"><he>שַׁרְיָא</he></cite>. Targ. II Esth. III, 8 <he>יומא ש׳</he> a permitted day (free for trade).—
<cite ref="Beitzah 3b:2">Bets. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>לדידי אפי׳ … ש׳</he> according to my opinion it is permitted even on the first day.
<cite ref="Beitzah 22a:17">Ib. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>אפי׳ בשבת ש׳</he> it is permitted even on the Sabbath.
<cite ref="Nedarim 62a:10">Ned. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ ליה לאינש לאודועי וכ׳</he> a man is permitted to make himself known (as a scholar) in a place where they do not know him; a. fr.

senses.gloss: [to loosen the girdle,] to sit down for a meal; trnsf. to start, begin.
units: Targ. Deut. XVI, 9 (O. ed. Berl. תְּשָׁרֵי, Pa.). Targ. II Esth. III, 7; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> (<cite ref="T00152"><he>רבתי</he></cite>) <he>כמה דשְׁרִין למיכל</he> (ed. Wil. <he>דשְׁרוֹ</he>) when they sat down to eat.
Y. Dem. I, 21ᵈ bot.; Y. Shek. V, 48ᵈ top שַׁרְיַית מנהקה (not שוריית) she began to bray; a. fr.—Trnsf. (cmp. meanings of b. h. יָאַל Hif.) to consent, be willing.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Joshua 7:7">Targ. Josh. VII, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Joshua 17:12">Ib. XVII, 12</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 6:9">Targ. Job VI, 9</cite>; <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 6:28">28</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 26:5">Targ. I Sam. XXVI, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 2:2">Targ. Num. II, 2</cite>, sq.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 40:35">Targ. Ex. XL, 35</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 16:8">Targ. Ps. XVI, 8</cite>, sq.; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:35">Y. Ter. VIII, 46ᵃ</cite> <he>חמריא שרון וכ׳</he> ass-drivers took lodging in an inn.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:1">Lam. R. to I, 1</cite> <he>רבתי אשכח … שרון יתבין וכ׳</he> (<he>חד מירוש׳</he>) he found men that had taken lodging there, and sat eating and drinking.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14:3:7">Y. Sabb. XIV, 14ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ע״י דהוה ש׳ תמן וכ׳</he> because he lived there (in Babylonia) &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20:12">Gen. R. s. 20</cite> <he>ויתיר … שרי</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01531"><he>פָּרָא</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 39a:11">Snh. 39ᵃ</cite> <he>כל בי … שָׁרְיָא</he> the Shechinah dwells wherever ten persons are assembled; a. fr.
Targ. Ps. XXX, 12 (ed. Wil. Pe.).
Targ. Job XII, 18 (ed. Wil. מַשְׁרֵי Af.); a. e.
Targ. O. Deut. I, 5 (Y. שׁוֹרֵי Poel). Ib. II, 24 (O. ed. Vien. Pe.). Ib. 25.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 4:31">Targ. Jer. IV, 31</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 13:12">Targ. Prov. XIII, 12</cite> <he>דמְשָׁרֵי למעדריה</he> (not <he>משדי</he>, v. Pesh. a. LXX) who begins to help himself (h. text <he>תחלת ממשכה</he>!).

senses.gloss: to cause to encamp or dwell, to let rest.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 2:15">Targ. Gen. II, 15</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 7:7">Targ. Jer. VII, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 23:2">Targ. Ps. XXIII, 2</cite>.
Ib. LXXIV, 2 Ms. (ed. Pa.); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 67a">Sabb. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>הסנה</he> … <he>א׳ קודשא וכ׳</he> O thornbush! not because thou art higher than all other trees did the Lord let his Presence rest upon thee &c.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:9">Koh. R. to III, 9</cite>, end <he>כל … לא מַשְׁרִין וכ׳</he> (in the hereafter) they allow every one to dwell only with his fellow tradesmen; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:9">ib.</cite> beg. <cite ref="M03107"><he>מתרין</he></cite> (corr. acc.); a. e.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 5:27">Targ. Is. V, 27</cite>.—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 14">Lev. R. s. 14</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00067"><he>חֲבִילָא</he> II</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Yevamot 106a:6">Yeb. 106ᵃ</cite> <he>כי היכי דתִישְׁתְּרִי לעלמא</he> in order that she may be free to marry again.
<cite ref="Beitzah 2b:11">Bets. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>יו״ט בעלמא תשתרי</he> let it be permitted for use on any other Holy Day (not followed by the Sabbath); a. e.
